body: Binary notation uses two symbols, written as 0 and 1 in this archive. In common positional binary the places have weights one, two, four, eight and onward from right to left. The sequence 101 therefore represents one group of four, no groups of two, and one more, a total of five.

Two distinguishable states can represent the symbols, as with holes and unmarked positions on a punched card. The record needs a convention for where to start, which direction to read, how to group positions and whether a group encodes a number, a character or a measurement.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: The meaning of a bit sequence depends on the surrounding agreement about its boundaries and mapping. A photographed IBM card has its own historical code, while the Centauri raster uses other rules.
purpose: Introduce a two-state representation for later framing and image records.
